verdict.rationale: Alacritty documents scriptable window creation through `alacritty msg create-window` and IPC. Its config can set the shell's working directory, window dimensions and startup mode, so a script can open project-scoped terminal windows. It explicitly leaves tabs and splits to a window manager or multiplexer, so there is no first-party way to define a multi-pane session or layout that opens in one command. Missing for 10: a declarative session/workspace definition, split or tab layouts, per-window commands bundled in one invocation, and hands-on corroboration (the runtime probe could not exercise `alacritty msg`).

support.subject: As a power-user, I can define startup sessions and window layouts in config or scripts so a project workspace opens in one command

citations.quote: New windows can be created either by using the `CreateNewWindow` keybinding action, or by executing the `alacritty msg create-window` subcommand.
Directory the shell is started in.
Number of lines/columns (not pixels) in the terminal.
